problem: Indoor navigation needs a complete metric traversability map, but a single egocentric image sees only a small floor frustum. No standardized real-world benchmark exists for single-view BEV metric floormap completion, and prior map-completion work (OccAnt, MapEx, PIPE) uses multi-step observations, simulation, or deterministic/ensemble predictors.
motivation: Single-view BEV completion is a one-to-many Bayesian inverse problem, so downstream planners need a distribution over plausible layouts rather than a point estimate. A single-frame prior can be fused over time in multi-step navigation, but comparing deterministic, ensemble and generative models needs a common dataset, protocol and calibration-aware metrics.
key_idea: Release FlatLands, a 270k-observation, 17.6k-scene benchmark for single-view BEV floor completion with ID/OOD splits, and use it to show that conditional flow-matching generators with evidence clamping yield better-calibrated, boundary-localized uncertainty than deterministic models or seed ensembles.
insight: Best-of-K sampling from generative models beats all deterministic predictors, and the oracle-free Masked Energy Score confirms the ranking. The boundary-variance decomposition shows FM+XAttn puts variance on layout boundaries (interior/boundary ratio ~600x) while LaMa-Ensemble spreads variance over determined interiors (ratio 2.4x), so ensemble seed spread is a poor proxy for layout ambiguity. In the end-to-end RGB pipeline, the stochastic advantage vanishes because front-end depth/segmentation noise dominates. The cross-attention ablation shows the gain over plain FM comes from the auxiliary condition encoder, not cross-attention (MES 0.095 vs 0.096).
method: Task formulation: given one RGB image, infer a distribution over the unobserved BEV floormap on a 256x256 grid (about 0.039 m/px) conditioned on the observed floor F_obs and unobserved mask U, with observed cells hard-clamped.

Dataset construction: mesh-based synthesis from 6 sources (ZInD, ARKitScenes, MP3D, ScanNet, 3RScan, ScanNet++). 24 poses per scene at a 90° HFOV camera 1.25 m high, ray-occlusion visibility, four aligned binary maps (F_obs, U, F_gt, valid), filter on conditioning ratio >=0.10, scene-disjoint splits, ScanNet++ held out as OOD test.

Perception front-end: DepthPro metric depth plus SegFormer floor segmentation, back-projected with intrinsics and RANSAC floor-plane alignment into an egocentric BEV, for the end-to-end RGB-to-floormaps pipeline.

Baselines: 4 naive fills, deterministic U-Net/PConv-UNet/LaMa (masked BCE, threshold 0.5 plus clamp), LaMa-Ensemble (4 seeds), and pixel-space DDPM/DDIM, Flow Matching and FM+XAttn with CFG s=2, per-step evidence clamping and K=4 samples.
FM+XAttn: flow matching U-Net with an auxiliary condition encoder on [F_obs, U] and cross-attention at 64x64 and 32x32 resolutions (Heun, 25 steps).

Metrics: UMR (mismatch rate on the unobserved valid region), IoU/F1, Masked Energy Score (Jaccard-distance energy score for fidelity plus diversity), best-of-K IoU, per-pixel variance, and a boundary-vs-interior variance decomposition.

setting.backbone: U-Net, PConv-UNet, LaMa, LaMa-Ensemble, DDPM-U-Net diffusion, flow-matching U-Net, FM+XAttn (all trained from scratch on BEV maps); DepthPro and SegFormer as frozen front-end
setting.training_data: FlatLands train split: 215,342 observations from 5 sources (ZInD, ARKitScenes, MP3D, ScanNet, 3RScan); 300k steps, batch 64, 4xA100
setting.observation: single egocentric RGB image (end-to-end) or a BEV observed-floor map plus unobserved mask (benchmark protocol)
setting.action_space: none (perception/mapping task: outputs binary BEV floor maps)
setting.simulator: none; offline synthesis from real scanned meshes (Matterport3D, ScanNet, etc.)
setting.privileged: Benchmark protocol conditions on GT mesh-derived BEV observation (F_obs, U); the end-to-end setting uses estimated depth and segmentation only

numbers_note: No navigation benchmarks. Results are on the paper's own FlatLands benchmark. The official split is only called 'test', with ID/OOD partitions. The CFG and K-sensitivity tables are described as calibrated interpolations, so they are not reported.
results: On FlatLands, all stochastic generators with best-of-4 beat every deterministic predictor: ID IoU is 0.830 for FM+XAttn and Diffusion against 0.763 for U-Net. FM+XAttn has the best MES (ID 0.133, OOD 0.095) and puts variance at layout boundaries, unlike LaMa-Ensemble (MES 0.158/0.149). Method ranking is preserved OOD on ScanNet++. In the end-to-end RGB pipeline the stochastic advantage vanishes: FM+XAttn IoU 0.565 vs U-Net 0.564.
limitations: Binary traversability only, with no semantics or graded traversability, and simplified pinhole intrinsics.
Generative samplers are 20-80x slower than deterministic models (FM+XAttn about 6.7 s per observation), and no closed-loop navigation or planning evaluation is done.
Under heavy occlusion all methods leak floor across boundaries, and LaMa collapses; the end-to-end evaluation is small (N=1000) and shows no stochastic advantage.
